questions.prompt: In Fortran, how are 2D arrays `A(i, j)` laid out in memory?

options.text: Column-major: the first index `i` varies fastest in contiguous memory

code.source:
do j = 1, n
  do i = 1, m
    a(i, j) = 0.0
  end do
end do

questions.prompt: What does an assumed-shape dummy argument `real, intent(in) :: a(:)` allow?

options.text: Accepting any 1D array or non-contiguous slice while passing shape metadata automatically (requires an explicit interface)

questions.prompt: What does the `pure` prefix on a Fortran `function` or `subroutine` enforce?

options.text: No side effects (cannot modify global/module variables, do I/O, or call impure procedures)

questions.prompt: Select all properties of an `elemental` procedure in Fortran. (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Written for scalar arguments, but can be called on arrays of any rank element-wise

code.source:
elemental real function sq(x)
  real, intent(in) :: x
  sq = x * x
end function sq

questions.prompt: Match each Fortran procedure modifier or attribute to its guarantee.

columns.label: Dummy argument cannot be modified inside the procedure
Caller's value is ignored on entry and must be assigned before return
Procedure has no side effects on global state or I/O

questions.prompt: How do you check whether an `optional` dummy argument was provided by the caller?
What does `use my_mod, only: compute, RealKind` accomplish?

options.text: Imports only the listed symbols, preventing namespace pollution and name clashes

questions.prompt: What is the default visibility of entities in a Fortran `module` if neither `public` nor `private` is specified?

options.text: `public` (best practice is to put `private` at the top and explicitly list `public :: ...`)

questions.prompt: What does `type :: Vec2` with `real :: x, y` define, and how are its fields accessed?

code.source:
type :: Vec2
  real :: x, y
end type Vec2

questions.prompt: What is a subtle trap when writing `real, save :: total = 0.0` vs `real :: total = 0.0` inside a Fortran procedure?

options.text: Initializing a local variable in its declaration (`real :: total = 0.0`) implicitly gives it the `save` attribute (persisting across calls)!

questions.prompt: What does `open(newunit=u, file='out.txt', status='replace', action='write', iostat=ios, iomsg=msg)` avoid?

options.text: Hardcoding unit numbers like `10` that could collide with other open files (`newunit` picks an unused unit safely)

questions.prompt: What does `iostat=ios` return when `open` or `read` succeeds vs hits end-of-file?

options.text: `0` on success, negative (`iostat_end`) on EOF, and positive on error

questions.prompt: What is an 'internal file' in Fortran I/O (`write(str, '(I0)') num` or `read(str, *) val`)?

options.text: Using a `character` string variable as the unit in `read`/`write` to format or parse strings

questions.prompt: Select all true statements about `character(len=:), allocatable :: s` (deferred-length strings). (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Eliminates fixed-buffer truncation and manual padding

questions.prompt: What does `where (a > 0.0) b = sqrt(a)` do?

options.text: Applies `b = sqrt(a)` masked element-wise only where `a > 0.0` is `.true.`

questions.prompt: What does `pointer` + `target` require in Fortran (`p => x`)?

options.text: Any variable can be pointed to
The target `x` must be declared with the `target` (or `pointer`) attribute so the compiler knows aliasing is possible

questions.prompt: What is the difference between `p => x` and `p = x` when `p` is a Fortran `pointer`?

options.text: `p => x` associates pointer `p` to point at `x`; `p = x` copies `x`'s value into what `p` currently points to

questions.prompt: What does `interface operator(+)` or `interface solve` inside a module define?

options.text: Operator overloading or generic procedure overloading resolved at compile time by argument types/ranks

questions.prompt: What does `allocate(b, source=a)` or `b = a` (reallocation on assignment) do for allocatable arrays?

options.text: Allocates `b` with `a`'s shape and copies `a`'s values (deep value semantics)

questions.prompt: Match each Fortran array concept to its syntax.
What does `do concurrent (i = 1:n)` communicate to the Fortran compiler?

options.text: Iterations are independent (no loop-carried dependencies), allowing SIMD vectorization, threads, or GPU offload

questions.prompt: What does `move_alloc(from=tmp, to=arr)` do in modern Fortran?

options.text: Transfers the allocated buffer ownership from `tmp` to `arr` in O(1) without copying, leaving `tmp` unallocated

questions.prompt: What is a `namelist` (`namelist /sim_params/ dt, nsteps`) used for in scientific Fortran?

options.text: Reading and writing human-readable key-value configuration blocks directly from/to text files

questions.prompt: What does `recursive function fact(n) result(res)` require in Fortran 90-2008 (and default in 2018)?

options.text: The `recursive` keyword (and `result(res)` when calling itself) in pre-2018 standards; Fortran 2018 makes procedures recursive by default unless `non_recursive`

questions.prompt: Select all valid `intent` attributes in Fortran. (Select all that apply.)
What does the `value` attribute on a dummy argument (`integer, value :: n`) do?

options.text: Passes a local copy by value (useful for C interop and preventing aliasing)

questions.prompt: What does `contiguous` on an assumed-shape dummy argument (`real, intent(in), contiguous :: a(:)`) tell the compiler?

options.text: `a` is guaranteed to be contiguous in memory, enabling optimal SIMD vectorization (compiler copies if caller passes a non-contiguous slice)

questions.prompt: What does `minloc(a)` / `maxloc(a)` return?

options.text: An integer array (or scalar with `dim=`) giving the index location of the minimum/maximum element

questions.prompt: What does `pack(a, mask = a > 0.0)` return?

options.text: A 1D array containing only the elements of `a` where `a > 0.0` is true

questions.prompt: What does `count(a > 0.0)` return?

options.text: The number of `.true.` elements in the logical mask `a > 0.0`

questions.prompt: Select all true statements about Fortran `associated(p)` vs `allocated(a)`. (Select all that apply.)

options.text: They are interchangeable on the same variable
`allocated(a)` checks whether an `allocatable` variable currently holds memory
`associated(p)` checks whether a `pointer` is associated with a target
Calling `associated(p)` on an undefined (uninitialized) pointer is invalid—always initialize pointers with `=> null()`

questions.prompt: What does `use, intrinsic :: iso_fortran_env` provide?
What happens in Fortran if you pass a non-contiguous slice `A(1, :)` to an `explicit-size` dummy array `real :: x(n)`?

options.text: The compiler may silently create a temporary contiguous copy-in/copy-out (which can hurt performance on hot paths)

questions.prompt: What does `block ... end block` (Fortran 2008+) allow inside a procedure?

options.text: Scoping local variables and `allocatable`s to a smaller block than the entire procedure

questions.prompt: Match each Fortran intrinsic to its operation.

columns.label: Extracts elements matching mask `m` into a 1D array
Transfers allocatable ownership in O(1) without copying

questions.prompt: What does `inquire(file='data.bin', exist=ok)` check?

options.text: Sets logical `ok` to `.true.` if `'data.bin'` exists on disk

questions.prompt: Why is `access='stream', form='unformatted'` useful for binary file I/O in modern Fortran?

options.text: Reads/writes raw unformatted bytes without Fortran's legacy record-length markers, matching C/NumPy binary files

questions.prompt: What does `fpm test` do in an `fpm` project?

options.text: Compiles and runs all test executables in `test/`

questions.prompt: What does `associate (x => sim%grid%pressure)` do?

options.text: Binds a short alias `x` to a long expression/component within an `associate ... end associate` block

code.source:
associate (p => sim%grid%pressure)
  p = p * 0.5
end associate

Select all ways to prevent silent numeric precision bugs in Fortran. (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Use `real(real64)` from `iso_fortran_env` and suffix literals with `_real64`

questions.prompt: What does `get_command_argument(1, arg)` (and `command_argument_count()`) do?

options.text: Retrieves CLI arguments passed to the Fortran executable
